column6: Definition & Botanical Description
A vine-grown herbaceous plant producing long, green-skinned fruits with white flesh, typically harvested immature.
A tropical perennial plant grown for its edible purple or green elongated fruits with a spongy texture.
A climbing annual plant known for its remarkably long green pods, harvested as a vital legume source.
An annual leafy crop cultivated primarily for salads, known for crisp leaves and high water content.
A mucilaginous flowering plant valued for its fibrous, seed-containing green pods.
A sprawling vine that bears large, hard-skinned yellow/orange fruits rich in Vitamin A and carbohydrates.
A cylindrical, ridged fruit vegetable harvested young for food or dried maturely for industrial loofah sponges.
A leafy vegetable forming a compact, elongated head with broad white ribs and light green leaves.
A rugose, bitter-tasting green pod vegetable celebrated for its medicinal properties and blood sugar management.
A premium global export banana variety, sweet and smooth, consumed fresh upon ripening.
A triploid hybrid cooking banana variety with thick, starchy square fruits widely used in local cuisine.
A savory, juicy red fruit vegetable rich in lycopene, acting as a foundational culinary base.
A cylindrical, high-moisture green creeping vine fruit widely consumed fresh for cooling properties.
An edible macroscopic fungus variety (e.g., Oyster, Straw) grown under controlled substrate conditions.
A small, pungent, highly spicy native chili cultivar widely used to introduce heat to dishes.
A sweet, fragrant round fruit with dynamic orange or green flesh and a high juice content.
A major woody shrub root crop containing high starch content, requiring processing to eliminate cyanogenic glycosides.
An erect, non-heading green leaf cabbage with smooth, spoon-shaped leaves and crisp white petioles.
A semi-aquatic tropical trailing vine cultivated on land for its tender, nutrient-dense leaves and hollow stems.
A pungent, slightly bitter cruciferous green leaf variety with ruffled edges, often preserved.
An elongated, mild-to-moderately spicy green pepper frequently utilized as an aromatic base in stews.
A temperate annual leafy herb rich in iron and vitamins, increasingly grown in highland areas.
A small, intensely sour indigenous citrus fruit with a green-to-yellow peel, central to regional gastronomy.
A coarse, aromatic perennial grass emitting a strong citrus aroma from its essential oils.
A succulent, smooth-leaved mucilaginous vine with red or green stems, highly resilient to tropical heat.
A 'superfood' tree crop with small oval leaflets globally recognized for exceptional multi-vitamin profiles.
A pungent underground rhizome featuring zesty, warming essential oils used extensively in cooking and traditional healing.
Large, blocky, sweet-fleshed non-pungent peppers available in vibrant red, yellow, and green varieties.
A cool-season crop where dense, compact white flower clusters (curds) form the primary edible structure.
A highly nutritious trailing root crop producing sweet, starchy tubers varying from white to deep orange.
An elongated, crisp white root vegetable presenting a sharp, peppery bite due to sulfur compounds.
A high-sugar maize variant harvested at the milk stage to preserve tender, sweet kernels.
A perennial bunching onion harvested for its long, hollow green leaves and mild bulb base.
The tender terminal vine tips of the sweet potato plant, consumed as an iron-rich leafy green.
Refers to traditional, heritage varieties of sweet potato cultivated locally for immediate food security.
An annual subterranean legume cultivated for its high-protein, oil-rich seeds enclosed in a fibrous pod.
A pungent, deep purple-red layered bulb crop essential as a primary savory aromatic foundation across cuisines.
A highly mucilaginous leafy green shrub known for heat tolerance; also source of industrial jute fiber.
A multi-sided legume with prominent wavy frills along four edges, entirely edible from root to leaf.
A close relative of the banana endemic to the Philippines, prized globally for yielding the strongest natural leaf fibers.
An exquisite fiber extracted from the long leaves of specific pineapple cultivars (e.g., Red Spanish).
A soft, fluffy seed-case fiber that grows in a protective boll around the seeds of the cotton plant.
A luxurious, continuous protein fiber filament produced by the silkworm cocoon during pupation.
A resilient, wild screwpine species with long thorny leaves harvested and prepared for heavy-duty weaving.
An indigenous shrub with incredibly tough bast bark fibers used for high-performance specialty papers.
A versatile fiber obtained via stripping the membrane on the underside of the fronds of the Raffia palm.
A massive fan palm yielding multiple fiber types (Buri, Raffia, Agas) from its broad, durable fronds.
The coarse, fibrous material extracted from the outer husk of the coconut fruit, highly resistant to rot.
A succulent monocot yielding long, stiff, durable structural fibers from its sword-like leaves.
An Agave species widely naturalized locally, yielding fine, flexible fibers via saltwater retting.
A robust Agave relative specialized for arid regions, producing thick, hard structural fibers.
A flue-cured tobacco variety characterized by high sugar content and bright golden leaves.
An air-cured, low-sugar tobacco variety presenting chocolate flavors and high nicotine absorption capacity.
Sun-cured local heritage cultivars traditionally processed into strong local leaf formats.
Heavy, robust tobacco variety cured slowly without direct heat, developing deep dark leaf profiles.
A large, mild, sweet layered onion bulb variety with golden-white skin, favored for raw use.
Small clustered bulb species producing intense, sharp, refined savory profiles widely used in native sauces.

A cultivar of the common onion (Allium cepa) characterized by its crisp, mildly pungent, and slightly sweet flavor. It is instantly recognizable by its papery, deep purplish-red outer skin and white rings tinged with red.
A crisp, sweet root vegetable with bright orange flesh exceptional in beta-carotene and structural crunch.
A round, leafy head vegetable with tightly overlapping leaves, thriving in elevated highland zones.
The tender, edible green pods of the common bush bean, crunchy and widely cultivated in cool highlands.
A major starchy tuber crop fundamental to global food security and extensively utilized as a recipe thickener.
A strongly pungent bulb crop rich in allicin, serving as the definitive foundational aromatic for sautéing.
The 'Tree of Life' fruit crop, harvested for its edible meat, hydrating water, and highly valuable commercial oil.
A juicy, sweet tropical compound fruit renowned for its striking crown of leaves and high bromelain content.
The national fruit of the Philippines, internationally acclaimed for its exceptionally sweet, non-fibrous golden flesh.
A large, spike-covered fruit famous for its powerful aroma and rich, custard-like, highly decadent flesh.
An understory tree crop yielding large pods containing beans processed into chocolate and cocoa solids.
A brilliant purple yam cultivar displaying deep violet flesh, highly sought after for global dessert applications.
A climbing cactus fruit showing vibrant pink skin with scaled bracts and speckled, refreshing flesh.
The largest wild citrus fruit species, exhibiting thick pith and crisp, sweet, mildly pink vesicles.
A local sweet orange hybrid with a glossy dark green rind and tart, deeply refreshing orange pulp.
A unique pear-shaped fruit highly valued for its creamy texture and rich content of monounsaturated fats.
A perennial crop harvested for its tender, crisp green spears before the foliage expands.
An endemic tree nut boasting a remarkably rich, buttery kernel enclosed in a hard, smooth shell.
A bright red tropical fruit covered in soft, hair-like spines, revealing translucent, sweet arils.

A highly versatile, starchy cooking banana native to the Philippines. Shorter, thicker, and more angular than common dessert bananas (like the Cavendish), it features a thick peel and firm, white flesh.
An elongated, edible fruit produced by the world's largest herbaceous plant. It features a protective outer peel and soft, sweet, cream-colored flesh.
A widely cultivated vegetable (Allium cepa) with a sharp, pungent odor and taste. It consists of a round, underground bulb made of tightly layered fleshy leaves.

The harvested grain of the rice plant (Oryza sativa) with its protective, inedible outer husk (hull) still intact. It is the raw agricultural commodity. Once milled to remove the husk, it becomes bigas (milled white or brown rice), and once cooked, it is called kanin (steamed rice).
Palay crops grown in fields that require standing water for normal growth, where water is supplied via artificial irrigation systems.
Palay crops grown in fields that depend entirely on natural rainfall for their water supply, lacking any artificial irrigation setup

A versatile cereal grass and grain that serves as a fundamental staple food for humans, a primary feed source for livestock, and a raw material for various industrial products (like starch, oil, and biofuel)

Corn varieties with yellow-pigmented kernels, rich in beta-carotene (which gives it its warm yellow-orange color). It is the primary ingredient used in formulated feed mixes for poultry, hogs, and aquaculture. It is also processed into corn oil and cornstarch.

Corn varieties with white or cream-colored kernels, typically consisting of traditional "flint" or glutinous cultivars (such as the heirloom Tinigib variety). It is cracked and milled into coarse grits (bugas mais) to serve as a direct rice substitute and main food staple for millions of people, particularly in the Visayas and Mindanao. It is also eaten boiled on the cob or used in native desserts (kakanin).
